meta.about: Every lesson and rule harvested from the films, each with one destination in Slate (a code default, a gate with its tests, a skill rule, dropped with a reason, a gap with the change that closes it, or pending: being built now, with its planned file). `slate knowledge check` proves it against the checkout.

unchanged_since_the_first: FILMROOT/SOUND.md (its proof-3 notes were harvested the first time)
harvests.left_behind: FILMROOT/tools/layers/ and the website's HANDOFF.md and COMPONENTS.md: the website tooling (one dropped item, L-packaging-S001)

harvests.label: addendum
harvests.covers: the film session's work after the second harvest (2026-10-01 02:28) to its last change (04:06): plate timing repair, the refined count box, reviewing a proposed mix, slow tails moved to transforms, and the triage after the last stability pass

meta.next_harvest: once films B and C and the p3 sound are approved

lessons.text: Intake keeps the requester's message verbatim, every mid-goal message verbatim with what it changed, and one checklist row per requirement with its status and evidence; that checklist is the contract.

terms: Every ask in the requester's words
destination.note: slate new writes brief/GOAL.md: the request verbatim, a checklist row per ask with status and evidence; later messages go in verbatim (production.add_ask).

lessons.text: Supplied inputs (an original film, motion references) are copied into the film folder and sha256-verified before any tool reads them.

terms: Slate never replaces a supplied input
verify the copy byte for byte
destination.note: `slate film input <file> [--source WHO] [--as NAME]` copies it to brief/inputs/, checks the copy's SHA-256 against the source, records who supplied it in film.lock.json and locks it.

terms: checks the copy's SHA-256 against the source

lessons.text: After any summary or compaction, re-derive the checklist from the verbatim request, never from memory; items rebuilt from follow-up messages are marked as reconstructed.

terms: re-derive the checklist from the verbatim request, never from memory

lessons.text: Record the owner's calls on each script draft (trims, keeps, confirmations) as numbered decisions in the tracker.

terms: Record the owner's calls on each script draft

lessons.text: Before building, compare the candidate production routes (for example generated versus built in code or AE), recommend one, and timebox a test of the strongest alternative.

terms: compare the candidate routes for the film
timebox a test of the strongest alternative

lessons.text: A build-gate table lists every open decision with its status in the owner's own words and where it's answered; nothing is built until the owner says go on script, look, voice and route.

destination.note: The pre-production sitting (checklist, claims, script, voice shortlist, look test) blocks a supervised film; `slate status` shows it as @preproduction and names what's waiting. The production route is chosen and recorded per orchestration.md.

lessons.text: Every owner correction is logged verbatim as a numbered direction change, then fixed in a targeted way: re-voice only the changed lines with neighbour context, redraw, re-render the range, splice, re-QA, re-mix, rebuild AE, re-master and re-validate.

terms: logged verbatim as a numbered direction change

lessons.text: Superseded material is archived with a README (path, what it was, what superseded it); earlier deliveries are never touched.

terms: A delivered version is never overwritten

lessons.text: Human approval points are explicit and blocking: the goal checklist, the source of truth, the script and later truth corrections, the production route, the voice (by ear), sound proofs (by ear), the look, hero moments, generated plates, spend beyond prepaid balances, the scope of fidelity passes, and the final review.

terms: Human approval points across a production
The scope of a fidelity pass

lessons.text: An autonomy grant covers creative decisions only; purchases, upgrades and spend past a prepaid balance still need an explicit yes, and when a quota runs out the work stops.
Record every autonomy grant with its scope and every approval of machine use (a render machine, offloading files, quieting services).

terms: Record an autonomy grant with its scope in the owner's words
destination.note: `slate approve grant --scope "…" --by NAME`, an approval of kind 'grant' (the owner's words, hashed in brief/grants/); `slate status` lists every grant. The films' machine-use approvals were for the retired second machine.

terms: Record every autonomy grant with its scope

lessons.text: Parallel production shape that worked: act builders who each own their files, one sound designer working in parallel, a separate timeboxed alternative track, and central finals and central sound.

terms: one sound designer working in parallel

lessons.text: Trackers restate every ask in the requester's own words (ask, status, evidence), number each direction change with its quote and what it supersedes, say 'latest approvals govern', and keep a turn log, spend by balance, the delivery bar and a dated status log.

destination.note: PRODUCTION.md keeps the asks in the requester's words, numbered verbatim direction changes (the latest approval governs), questions, revisions, approvals and a status table; spend by balance lives in the ledger.

lessons.text: Status keys: done means verified with named evidence; a shot is done only when built, rendered, validated and QA-passed; proofs are not completed shots.

destination.note: An ask can't be marked done without named evidence; stage statuses come from `slate status`, where a proof is not a finished stage.

also.note: Enforced by construction: an ask can't be marked done without evidence (tests/state/test_production.py::test_asks_messages_and_marks); stage statuses come from slate status, where a proof is not a finished stage.

lessons.text: Generated files carry 'do not edit by hand: <command>' and readable docs render between markers; edits go to the source and the tool reruns.
Delegate research to sub-agents with sourced briefs: a character's philosophy into a voice brief, a motion spec from real references, a capability brief where every line carries a source.

terms: Research can be delegated the same way

lessons.text: Approved takes and plates are reused, never regenerated; new lines are voiced at the same delivery with neighbours as context.
Get a first working version of every shot onto disk fast and keep NOTES.md current: builder sessions end without warning, and one lost unsaved work.

terms: Get a first working version of every shot onto disk quickly

lessons.text: Never move or archive files that running agents read; clean up only after the builders finish.

terms: Never move, rename or archive files that running agents read

lessons.text: The visionary bar: every act gets one signature moment that could make someone cry, inside the brand's own visual language (no glows, flares, particles or bounce); correct but ordinary fails, and hero moments are reviewed against the bar.

Intentionality degrades across parallel versions: tie every move to a word or idea, prefer fewer and better moves, judge new work against the best prior film's code and notes, and hold masters until the pass is done.
Process knowledge that lives only in prose (trackers, NOTES.md, memory notes) is lost unless it's encoded as rules, checks and defaults; the knowledge ledger maps every lesson to one.

destination.note: `slate knowledge check` proves every harvested lesson lands on a code default, a gate with its tests or a skill rule, and fails while any is unmapped, a gap or pending.

lessons.text: Ship the data model as versioned JSON schemas: film.json, script and storyboard, VO cues and words, shots, events, timeline, visual events, sound cues, mix records, captions, QA records, joins, renders registry, validation, manifest, plate selections, generation manifests, score plans and takes.

destination.note: Every film file has a versioned JSON schema in src/slate/schemas/ (film, script, storyboard, shots, vo_cues, vo_words, events, timeline, visual events, sound cues, mix, captions, gates, renders registry, manifest, plates, score), checked through jsonio.validate.

lessons.text: Encode the production method as a workflow with blocking human approvals: goal, toolchain proof, analysis, truth, motion law, treatment and script, build gate, voice by ear, timing, look test, kit and brief, plates, parallel builders, central finals, QA, sound and score, mix, captions, AE, masters, validation, delivery and the review loop.

terms: The production method is a workflow with blocking human approvals

lessons.text: Keep briefs in sync with what was built: one brief still said two shots were built in AE after they'd been rebuilt in code.

terms: Keep briefs in sync with what was built

lessons.text: Generate docs from data (spotting sheets, sound tables) between markers so they can't drift; hand-written docs had already drifted from the code (ducking depths).

destination.note: Readable docs render between markers from the data: GOAL.md and PRODUCTION.md (slate.state), a brand's MOTION.md from brand.json (slate.brand.motiondoc).

lessons.text: The fast lane (a narrated explainer built from 10 s blocks with one style key, or a quick generated clip) is used only when someone picks it at the front door's question, and never for brand work: stylized generated clips aren't the brand's type or real UI.
Orphaned intermediates that nothing reads (a raw cue sheet, unpaced Whisper output).

destination.reason: Nothing consumes them: `slate make` builds only the files in its dependency graph, so these intermediates are never made.

lessons.text: When a decision changes (for example where renders run), update or retire the memory notes and docs that state the old rule; two notes still sent renders to a retired machine.
Each film folder is git-initialized for its small files (heavy media ignored) and lives outside iCloud; the source project wasn't a repo and had one Time Machine backup as its only copy.

destination.note: slate new starts a git repository for the film's small files (state/scaffold.py GITIGNORE keeps heavy media out) and warns when the film folder is inside iCloud Drive (state/film.py).

lessons.text: Harvest the per-act NOTES.md files (3,565 lines) and the character motion spec into the knowledge ledger in their own pass.

destination.note: The doc-rules harvest carries every act NOTES.md rule and the character motion spec, each with its id, and the ledger maps every one.

lessons.text: The source films' shapes (shot counts, runtimes, voices, builder counts, render machines and status on 2026-09-30).

destination.reason: Facts about the three source films (shot counts, runtimes, voices, builders, machines on 2026-09-30); the reusable parts are harvested as their own lessons.

lessons.text: A reference review lists what to keep and what to fix; common faults found were deck-like pacing, on-screen text repeating the VO, hard cuts, tiny body copy, a master 16 LU under target (-30.7 LUFS) and no call to action.

terms: What to keep and what to fix
destination.note: The reference review names these faults up front.

lessons.text: Reference analysis includes a table of claims in the reference that conflict with the brand's current website or product.

terms: in a table, for the claim authority
destination.note: The conflicts table stops stale claims being copied.

terms: decide each with the claim authority before writing

lessons.text: Truth research pins the product source at a commit, reads company code in place (git show, git grep) and cites path:line; the website, live app pages, public demos and guidelines are read and cited too.

terms: read in place at a pinned commit
read and cited with the date
destination.note: Pinned, cited sources can be re-checked later.

lessons.text: The owner names the source of truth for product claims; retired prototypes and demos are layout references only.

terms: The owner names the source of truth for product claims

lessons.text: Before build, re-verify every quoted product fact against the pinned source and correct its path:line; about 110 quotes were re-checked this way.

destination.note: Run by check_plan before the build: each quoted product fact re-read at its pinned commit (read-only git), naming the line it moved to when it's found nearby.

also.note: Stated as a rule, and gated: script.quotes re-reads each quoted fact at the pinned commit.

lessons.text: The script has one hand-edited data source; the readable script and storyboard are generated from it and carry a 'do not edit here' note.

destination.note: SCRIPT.md and the storyboard are generated from script.json and stamped.

terms: is the only hand-edited script file

lessons.text: A treatment covers the idea as a reframe, runtime rationale (why not shorter or longer), act by act, an emotional arc, one signature moment per act, the character's gesture vocabulary, voice direction, look and sound, what the film never shows, the owner's calls, and notes for builders.
Script gate: VO at or under 2.6 words per second in every shot.

destination.note: The format can lower the 2.6 ceiling.

lessons.text: Script gate: on-screen read time is estimated as hold >= max(1.5 s, 0.4 s + 0.3 s x words) against settle-to-exit time (approximated as duration minus the entrance and 0.75 of the entrance for the exit).
Script gate: no banned word appears in the on-screen text, the picture notes or the VO.
Script gate: runtime within +-10% of the target runtime unless the brief justifies otherwise.

destination.note: The target comes from film.json or the format's range.

lessons.text: Script gate: no dashes in VO lines.

destination.note: A script rule (rules.vo_dashes: fail or review), so a brand can switch it off.

lessons.text: Script gate: every shot carries a truth source (code path:line, website, the reference film's scene, or an owner ruling).

destination.note: On when the script sets rules.every_shot_sourced.

lessons.text: Script gate: at most 12 on-screen words per shot.
A brief can pin required lines (for example a character's fixed opening line) and the script gate checks they're present and unchanged.

destination.note: The pinned opening line is data (rules.first_line), not code.

lessons.text: The script generator exits non-zero with a problem list and writes nothing when any check fails.

terms: when nothing fails and this isn't a check
destination.note: A failing build writes nothing and keeps the last good storyboard (tests/story/test_story_build.py).

lessons.text: Each script draft carries a human-readable change note in its version (date and whose corrections).

terms: the change note for this draft

lessons.text: Each shot records an entrance-duration token so the read-time check can estimate when on-screen text settles.

destination.note: Each shot's enter_token is priced from the brand's duration scale.

lessons.text: The script generator renumbers shot ids and remaps every id mentioned in the text; once any scene uses the ids, renumbering is refused.

destination.note: Renumbering remaps mentions (story/model.py::remap_text); frozen ids refuse a renumber once scenes use them.

lessons.text: The script can declare a narrator and a character's gesture vocabulary with one meaning per gesture.

destination.note: The treatment names the voice and the gestures; the brand's motif.gestures maps each meaning to the rig.

lessons.text: Product-truth doc template: pinned commit, the product in one paragraph, journey order, screens and exact copy, the agent or character, secondary views, the product's own motion, palette and type, live versus not built, numbers and words to get right, and where the product disagrees with itself.

terms: where the product disagrees with itself

lessons.text: Capability brief template for a product character or agent: how it was checked, sources, what it knows, how it synthesizes and explains, what it suggests next, guardrails, what is NOT true, where this film differs, and what the film uses.

terms: Capability brief (for a product character or agent)
what is not true about it
where this film differs from the product

lessons.text: Propose the scope of a fidelity pass before widening it ('is this the pressing stuff?') and record the ruling: the product's core surfaces must match exactly, secondary surfaces need only feel right.
The product's code is the only product truth: it wins over docs, demos, prototypes and old films, and the owner's rulings win over the code for what's claimed.

terms: wins over docs, demos, prototypes and older films
The code wins over demos, docs and old films
the owner wins over the code for what's claimed
when a product demo's wording disagrees with the product's code, the code wins

lessons.text: Keep a per-brand 'never claim or show' list for things true in code but ruled out by the owner; the script gate, the builders' brief and the OCR scan all read it.

destination.note: The never-claim list (brand truth.never_claim plus the film's) fails the script anywhere it appears.

also.note: The same list is read against the frames' text at QA.

terms: What the film never shows or says

lessons.text: A number on screen or in the VO needs a current source or it's dropped; forward-looking claims appear only as the source said them.

destination.note: A forward-looking statement is a claim, so script.claims holds it to the approved list or a pinned source.

lessons.text: Never show as working anything that isn't built, is stubbed or is off by default; the product-truth doc's 'live versus not built' list feeds builders and checks.

terms: Never show as working anything that isn't built, is stubbed, or is off by default

lessons.text: Nothing is invented: every UI element, word and number maps to a citation; a concept screen needs explicit sign-off and a visible 'concept' treatment.

terms: maps to a citation in the truth pack
Never show UI the product doesn't have

lessons.text: Describe a product character only with capabilities the owner treats as true, and ground its gestures in the product's own motion with one meaning per gesture.

terms: Describe a character only with capabilities the owner treats as true
destination.note: Gestures: one meaning each, in the treatment.

lessons.text: On-screen text stays at or under 40% of the shot's VO words.

destination.note: At most 40% of the voice's words on screen (read-along text and a declared `reading` excepted); the default is src/slate/story/inputs.py:DEFAULT_READ_TIME.

terms: about 40% of what the voice says
also.note: Stated as a rule, and gated: script.on_screen caps the ratio at 40%.

terms: about 40% of the words the voice says in that shot

lessons.text: Script content lives in script.json, and the script checks read the brand's rules; one film's generator held its content in code and hard-coded a fixed opening line and a banned word.

destination.note: The content lives in script.json; the checks read the brand's pack, never a hard-coded line or word.

lessons.text: Extracting a website's copy as leaf-text lines lets on-screen copy be checked against the brand's real words; the source tool couldn't run because its HTML parser wasn't installed.

destination.note: stdlib html.parser, nothing to install; read_website returns `copy` beside what it found.

lessons.text: Hero lines have at most 6 words and at most 2 appear per act.

destination.note: A shot's `hero_lines`, carried into storyboard.json (src/slate/story/builder.py).

terms: 6 words or fewer, at most two per act
also.note: Stated as a rule, and gated: script.hero_lines.

terms: hero lines are short (six words or fewer)

lessons.text: Reference analysis is one repeatable stage: Demucs vocal split, Whisper transcript with word timestamps, generation-side scene analysis, ffmpeg scene scores, change and settled frames, contact sheets and OCR, joined into one scenes file.

destination.note: `slate analyze <video>` runs the whole stage as one command: Demucs split, Whisper transcript with word times, ffmpeg scene scores with change and settled frames and contact sheets, OCR, measured eases, and a Higgsfield scene analysis joined when one was made.

lessons.text: Every reference analysis records a method table (step, what ran, output) so its results can be re-derived.

Each brand's motion law is written once: named eases with bezier and AE speed/influence values, duration tokens, stagger rules, morph techniques, blur settings, the read-time rule, a banned list with reasoned exceptions and per-shot motion QA.

terms: A brand MOTION.md and its motion law
a banned list with reasoned exceptions

lessons.text: Look development runs moodboards first, then the same moodboards grounded in the brand kit, then moving look tests; several looks were rejected before one was accepted.

terms: A moving 10 to 15 second look-and-motion test

lessons.text: The owner picks the look from a moving test; colour or opening decisions that are still open are held for their own look test.
Research doc template: a source table, every claim with its source, the brand system (logos, fonts, colour tokens by source, UI patterns, icons, voice, motion tokens), conflicts and open questions.

Build a brand's look from its own design language (its site's or app's components and tokens), not generic prompts, and get a short moving look test approved before rolling it out; generic looks were rejected four times (flat shapes that didn't look polished, a 3D filament with no hierarchy, glossy futuristic glass, generated imagery that read as AI).

terms: Generic looks were rejected four times
approved from a short moving test

lessons.text: A brand pack defines the product's own palette tokens and font weights; logos keep their artwork colours; logo clear space and marks (registered, trademark) follow the brand's guidelines.

Brand, UI and video material goes to generators only when the owner allows it; company source code never leaves its machine (it's read in place); credentials are never uploaded, printed or written to files.

terms: goes to a generator only when the brand's owner allows it

lessons.text: Some brands forbid self-commentary on graphics (no 'Illustration' or 'Example' captions); make it a per-brand setting, because one film tagged a frame 'Illustration' against its own website's rule.

destination.note: A per-brand setting (brand.schema.json truth.self_commentary, default true): when it's false the script gate (script.banned_words) and qa's banned_words ban "Illustration" and "Example" captions on screen; the voice may still say them.

lessons.text: All script and research content from the source films (storyboards, scripts, treatment, product-truth and research docs, the voice brief, per-shot QA notes) is one brand's content.

destination.reason: One brand's own scripts, research and QA notes: they stay with that brand's private pack or the film project; Slate keeps only the templates (slate-story, slate-brand).

lessons.text: One brand's truth rules (its tier words, banned phrases, its character's untrue features, excluded logos and removed statistics).

destination.reason: One brand's truth data (its words, phrases and exclusions): Slate supports a truth pack per brand (brand.json truth) without shipping any.

lessons.text: The source films' sample company, people and numbers.

destination.reason: One brand's sample data: it belongs in that brand's pack (truth.sample_data), which the kit and the gates read.

lessons.text: One brand's palette, licensed font kit, logos and icons.

destination.reason: One brand's design system (palette, licensed font kit, logos, icons): it lives in that brand's private pack, never in the core (ARCHITECTURE section 1).

lessons.text: The paper 2.5D look (cards with real thickness, soft layered shadows, ghost pages, gentle camera) becomes a library look used only when a brand's own design language is papery; the source brand's colours and signature line stay with that brand.

destination.note: A library look chosen only when a brand's own design language is papery; the default for a brand that hasn't chosen is flat.

lessons.text: The source eases' lineage from one brand's CSS motion tokens: the method (derive eases from the product's own tokens and measured references) generalizes, the numbers stay in that brand's pack.

destination.note: The method (eases derived from the product's own tokens and measured references, with lineage) is Slate's; the source brand's numbers stay in its pack.

lessons.text: The source films' characters and signature moments (a logo-build hero moment, a reveal, the gesture set, key lines).

destination.reason: One brand's characters and signature moments: story content for its films. The general lessons behind them are harvested on their own (the visionary bar, L-method-020; the character method, slate-motion).

lessons.text: The source films' reference inputs (the original film, two motion reference films, content maps, guides and captured app and web research).

destination.reason: One brand's reference inputs: a pack models the kinds (sources, UI references, reference films), not these files.

lessons.text: Split everything brand-specific into a brand pack (tokens, fonts, logos, character marks, ease lineage, look references, brand-kit and voice ids) and a truth pack (source pin, citations, banned words, never-show list, numbers, sample data, scope rulings); no brand constants stay in code.

destination.note: Everything brand-specific is data in a pack (brand.json) that every module reads through slate.brand.pack; tests/brand/test_brand_nobrand.py and engine/tests/kit/nobrand.test.ts keep brand constants out of code.

lessons.text: Brand logos compile from the brand pack's SVG manifest into kit data (class fills become currentColor, glyph groups are kept for write-ons); the source tool hard-coded one brand's files.

destination.note: The kit parses the pack's SVG (paths, transforms, fills from attributes, styles and class rules) and plans the build from it (core/logo.ts planLogoBuild); nothing is hard-coded per brand.

lessons.text: The brand pack declares font families, weights and sources (local files, Google Fonts or a kit URL) and FontGate verifies each declared face; the core ships open-licence defaults, because a brand's licensed font can't be redistributed.

destination.note: The pack declares families, weights, sources and licences; the kit's font plan loads each face and the FontGate (kit/fonts.tsx) fails on a missing or substituted face.

lessons.text: Only generic design queries go to third-party design-inspiration services; no brand or product material leaves the machine that way.

terms: Only generic design queries go to third-party inspiration services

lessons.text: Rebuild a brand's components for film at film scale rather than importing its website code; the films borrowed the website's look language, not its components.
A brand's signature motif keeps one colour through the film and changes form only at designed moments.

terms: A signature motif keeps one colour

lessons.text: A voice brief that quotes company code must not travel into a personal or public package.

terms: A voice brief that quotes company code

lessons.text: A brand's web font kit only serves allowed domains and loads online during renders; in AE the same fonts must be activated or installed separately.

terms: may serve only its allowed domains

lessons.text: One brand's frontend-taste skill moves to that brand's pack.

destination.reason: One brand's UI-taste skill moves to that brand's private pack; a pack carries its own skills (brands/_template/skills), never Slate's core.

lessons.text: A brand with no design system can bootstrap its pack with the generation vendor's brand-kit skill (palette, SVG marks, type, brandbook).

terms: bootstrap its pack with a brand-kit tool

lessons.text: Vendor brand-kit ids (used to ground voice and image generations) are brand-pack data, not secrets.

destination.note: Brand-kit ids live in the pack's grounding block (src/slate/schemas/brand.schema.json $defs.grounding), beside uploads_allowed; they aren't secrets.

lessons.text: HyperFrames' translation of a brand's design.md into camera-ready tokens is the same idea as a brand pack's tokens, made brand-agnostic.

destination.note: Slate's onboarding reads a brand's own design tokens from its CSS, scripts and SwiftUI (slate.brand.sources) into pack tokens with their sources; HyperFrames' design.md mapping is learn-from only (PLAN appendix A).

lessons.text: A private brand pack can ship as a plugin that depends on the core plugin (cross-marketplace dependencies need an explicit allow).

destination.reason: Not how the plan ships brand packs: they live in the separate brand store (PLAN decision 4, SLATE_BRANDS) and slate.brand.pack.find reads them there, so no plugin dependency is needed.

lessons.text: Never fetch a brand's licensed fonts from its web kit into a third-party sandbox; font licences cover specific uses.

terms: Never fetch a brand's licensed fonts from its web kit into a third-party sandbox

lessons.text: Video analysis on the generation vendor's platform costs no credits and returns a scene breakdown, so slate analyze uses it by default alongside ffmpeg scene scores.

destination.note: Joined when it was made: Higgsfield's video analysis is a hosted-connector tool (the chat lane), so the CLI takes its result with --higgsfield rather than calling it; ffmpeg scene scores always run.

lessons.text: Plan shot durations at 2.7 words per second of speech plus lead, tail and hold; re-derive them from the real takes once they exist.

destination.note: Shots are planned at the speech rate plus lead, tail and hold; `slate script build --from-takes` re-derives them from the real takes.

lessons.text: Timecodes are computed from durations and frame rounding, never typed by hand.

destination.note: SCRIPT.md's timecodes are computed from the plan's frame-rounded lengths, never typed.

lessons.text: Whisper each take with word timestamps and snap every word's start, including the first word of a take, to the take's energy onset within ±80 ms (a rise of at least 3 dB); an unsnapped first word once sat about 0.13 s before the voice was audible.

destination.note: Every word start, the first word of a take included, snaps to the strongest energy rise within ±80 ms (MIN_RISE_DB 3 dB on a 5 ms envelope).

lessons.text: Because every beat is keyed to words, a full re-voice re-times the film automatically; the renders and the mix still have to be rebuilt.

terms: a full re-voice re-times the film automatically

lessons.text: Shot boundaries use drift-free rounding: round each cumulative start to the master frame and take lengths as differences of rounded starts, recording every rounding.

destination.note: Each shot's cumulative start is rounded to the master frame and its length is the difference of rounded starts; every rounding is recorded (tests/story/test_timing_shots.py::test_rounding_is_drift_free).

lessons.text: Timing gate: shot frames are contiguous, start at 0 and end exactly at the film's total frames.

An event can be anchored to a spoken word (word, occurrence, offset); 'land' means 90% of travel, and the move's start is back-computed so the landing hits the word within +-2 frames; sound cues fire on the landing.

destination.note: A word anchor is {word, occ, offset}; "land" is ease:seconds and the resolver back-computes the start so 90% of travel hits the word (timing/ease.py t90).

lessons.text: The resolved timeline must not change once any act is rendered; the timeline tool is deterministic.

destination.note: The timeline locks once any act render is registered; re-timing then needs a person's force with a reason.

lessons.text: Picture and sound share one data flow: script -> takes and cues -> word timings -> shots -> timeline -> kit clock -> act compositions -> visual events -> sound cues -> stems and mix; captions come from words; renders -> QA -> AE -> masters -> validation -> manifest.

destination.note: slate make's graph is this data flow (script, voice, timing, events, renders, sound, master, deliver); STALE gate results follow the same inputs.

lessons.text: Word timings are stored relative to the take's first sample, with the script line and Whisper's heard text side by side; film time is the cue's frame over fps plus the word start.
frame_out is exclusive everywhere (shots, renders registry, render entries).

Allow documented timing exceptions (a character's anticipation beats land 3 to 6 frames before their word by design), each declared with its reason, and keep their sound locked to the picture within a frame.

destination.note: A declared exception (with its reason) turns a word-landing miss into a REVIEW item a person accepts, never a silent pass (tests/qa_core/test_qa_core_sync.py::test_word_landing_exception_is_review_until_a_person_accepts_it); the sound still lands on the picture beat (sound.cue_sync).

An audio tag is a short natural-language instruction in square brackets, placed where the delivery should change; the list is open, and eleven_v4 follows tags more reliably than earlier models, though not perfectly. v4 also supports instant clones (from about 10 s of audio) and professional clones.

Tag rules: don't tag every line (v4 infers emotion from well-written text); one emotion per phrase; a tag at the head of a line carries the whole line; tags describe something audible and fit the voice's character; if a line doesn't land, swap the tag rather than rewriting the words; never change a word.

lessons.text: Repetition gate, measured from rendered cues: longest identical run 1, no runs of three or more, no sound serving two kinds, at most 3 identical sounds in any second ('same' means log-mel fingerprint distance under 3 dB).

destination.note: The key, tempo, motif and materials are the brand pack's sound block; nothing is hard-coded for one character.

lessons.text: Dedupe windows per family: the same family within 40 ms merges, counts within 0.45 s, swells within 2.5 s, impacts within 1 s, and whooshes within the larger of 0.35 s and 45% of the previous move.

destination.reason: The retired v2 planner's dedupe windows (plan §2, "Left behind"); the effects engine is ported from the approved p3 pass and re-inventoried after proof 3.

lessons.text: Collisions within 35 ms: when both are tiny transients the lower-priority one drops, otherwise it's lowered 6 dB.

destination.reason: The retired v2 planner's collision rule (plan §2, "Left behind"); the p3 engine keeps proof 2's own spotting and is re-inventoried after proof 3.
