lessons.text: Judge a take with one picture per line: the current take above the candidate, as spectrograms (0-8 kHz) with the pitch contour, the level contour, the words and the measurements that decided the pick, on one shared time scale so length differences are real, drawn from the clean takes the metrics measured.

destination.note: One picture per comparison: every take on one time and colour scale, spectrogram, words, pitch and level contours and the measurements, drawn from the takes the metrics measured.

terms: every take on one time scale and one colour scale

lessons.text: Draw a key word's pitch for every take on one axis (log Hz), each with its start, peak, end and fall, and the voice's untagged takes in grey.

terms: The last word's pitch for several takes on one axis (log Hz
the last word's pitch for every take on one axis

lessons.text: Every voice measure is computed over the whole line and over the tag's scope (from the first word an emotion tag governs to the end of the line): a tag on the last word whispered that word while the line average barely moved.

destination.note: Measured over the whole line and from the tag's first word (tests/voice/test_voice_analyze.py::test_the_tag_scope_is_measured_from_its_first_word).

lessons.text: Verify a picture's axes with known signals before trusting it: the spectrogram's row and column mapping was checked with test tones.

destination.note: The spectrogram's rows (frequency, high at the top) and columns (time) are proven with 1, 2 and 5 kHz tones at known times, in the numbers and in the picture. Closed 2026-10-01.

lessons.text: Track each tagged line's status as approved (the exact take chosen by ear), proposed (a measured pick waiting for the ear) or current (the film take stays), in a machine-readable file beside the readable one; removing the tags gives back the script exactly.

destination.note: A round's picks are proposals (picks.json, with ranking.md beside it) until adopted; approved takes live in the voice manifest; tags strip back to the script exactly (slate.voice.tags.strip).

lessons.text: Accents over the score: every accent and impact, as mixed (ridden or not), at least 3 dB over the score in one of its own loudest third-octave bands over its loudest 120 ms.

Sync after the mix: every hit's anchor, measured again on the hit as mixed (ducked, split, ridden, limited), within one frame of its beat. The mix may move an anchor at most 10 ms and never to within 1 ms of its frame's edge; a hit already out of frame on its own is the spotting's fault, listed rather than failed as long as the mix didn't move it.

destination.note: Every effect's anchor is held within one frame of its beat; Slate's mix applies fixed gains and one linked limiter to the effects, so nothing rides a hit yet. Re-measuring each hit as mixed (the 10 ms and 1 ms rules) arrives with the guards (MIX-GUARDS, L-sound-S010).

lessons.text: Mix by family, not by stem: render each cue exactly as the engine renders it and send it to its family's bus, with per-hit clip gains (one gain for the whole hit, or one per side of a band split) set by the speech key's maximum over the hit's audible part, so a duck can never reshape a sound and move its sync (an early continuous duck moved one anchor 232 ms). Only reverb returns, long pads and plates duck continuously.

destination.what: mix by family: each cue to its family's bus with one clip gain per hit from the speech key, and sound/mix/family_stems/<family>.wav summing to the mix; tests: a duck doesn't move a hit's anchor, and the family stems sum to the mix
destination.note: waits for proof 3 (`slate approve proof3 <file> --by NAME`): the effects engine port; family stems come from its per-cue renders (NEEDS 213)

lessons.text: The speech key is the voice itself: a 20 ms RMS follower at a 1 kHz control rate against the voice's loud level (its 99th percentile), 0 at 40 dB under it and 1 at 25 dB under, held 150 ms across syllables, read 40 ms ahead so a duck is down before the first consonant, smoothed with an 8 ms attack and 250 ms release; swells use a slower key (40 ms attack, 600 ms release, 300 ms hold) so they move with phrases.

destination.what: the speech key: a 20 ms RMS follower on the voice against its loud level (0 at 40 dB under, 1 at 25 dB under), held 150 ms, read 40 ms ahead, 8 ms attack and 250 ms release; one clip gain per hit from its maximum over the hit's audible part
destination.note: waits for proof 3 (`slate approve proof3 <file> --by NAME`): the effects engine port; family stems come from its per-cue renders (NEEDS 213)

also.note: Today's key is an absolute one (0 under -40 dBFS RMS, 1 over -28) at 80 ms attack and 650 ms release, ducking the score only.

lessons.text: Split bands zero-phase: a 2nd-order Butterworth low-pass run forward and back, the top taken as the signal minus the low part, so the two sum back exactly and nothing moves in time.

destination.note: A 2nd-order Butterworth run forward and back; the voice's split takes its exact complement (band + rest == input).

lessons.text: The guards: after a first pass, measure every word; the clarity guard rides only the accents that really cover a word (on their top above 600 Hz, at most 15 dB, the whole hit if that isn't enough) and the air guard rides textures whole (at most 12 dB), solved together as the least total riding that clears every word, counting each hit's own reverb; then a second pass. A click on a word costs that word, and the word wins.

destination.what: the clarity, air and never-over guards solved together, the voice-as-delivered loop, approved spans frozen, anchors re-measured, and sound/mix/rides.json written (the balance gates, sound.balance.approved_spans and the listening file already read it)

lessons.text: A composed score gets its own clarity guard: where the score alone comes within 19 dB of the voice in 1-5 kHz during a word, its top above 600 Hz dips by just enough (at most 20 dB), held 0.15 s either side and ramped over 0.3 s so it moves at a phrase's pace. It keeps a quarter of the clarity budget so the accents keep the rest; a 1 kHz split barely reached the band's bottom octave. It also dips under an accent it would mask (in that hit's own bands for a low thump) and waits for a film's opening silence.

lessons.text: Every render gets one stability report: the glitch scan (one- and two-frame outliers) with motion triage, a step scan for persistent pops (something appears, vanishes or jumps and then holds: step(n) = d(n-1, n) - max(d(n-2, n-1), d(n, n+1)) per tile, with frames where most tiles step reported as cuts), and the jitter scan; every count is held to a limit that is zero for a final, and a failure is loud.

destination.note: One report per act render: the glitch scan with its motion triage, the step scan for pops and the motion scan's classes, each held to a limit of zero unless slate.toml says otherwise.

lessons.text: The jitter scan measures motion per 30 px tile at full resolution from 10-bit luma, to about 0.02 px, by two passes of Lucas-Kanade; a tile's motion counts only where it has texture, moves under 3 px a frame and the shift explains the change (or the tile barely changes); a straight edge vouches only for motion across itself; frames next to a cut aren't scored.

destination.note: 30 px tiles (TILE_PX) from 10-bit luma, two Lucas-Kanade passes (_lk_tiles), trusted only with texture (TEX), under 3 px a frame (FAST) and where the shift explains the change.

lessons.text: Jitter classes: snap (a slow rigid tile's move departs at least 0.45 px from its neighbours' agreeing moves and from a quadratic through n±2 and n±3, so an ease's tail scores 0); relative (two tiles moving as one object disagree by 0.35 px on one frame: text against its card); shake (three reversals in 7 frames, going nowhere); reversal (after steady travel, one whole-pixel step back); wobble (a near-still element steps a pixel and back within 4 frames: a count re-centring); flicker and shimmer at rest; and a veil (a faint one-frame change over many tiles: a band left out of one sub-frame). The floors sit just above the type tilt's quarter-pixel placement.
A reversal is a hard fail: no baseline accepts one, because a designed gesture never steps in whole pixels.

Baselines: a flag that is right by design (a gesture, a morph, a card swinging in fast) is triaged once by eye and accepted into the render's baseline, with the reason in the act's notes; from then on a flag that matches an accepted one (same class, within one frame and one tile) doesn't count, so the limits catch what is new. A baseline belongs to its act's content and is rewritten only after triage, when the act changes.

destination.note: `slate qa stability baseline` accepts what a person triaged; a baseline belongs to its act's content and survives re-renders of the same act.

lessons.text: Triage against a reference: run the same report on the reference render; flags it shares (same class, within 2 frames and one tile) belong to the design or were there before, and the rest are listed by class and frame for a look by eye. A one-sample reference has no motion blur, so fast moves flag differently there.

destination.note: Flags a reference render shares (same class, within 2 frames and one tile) are the design's (tests/qa_stability/test_qa_stability_scans.py::test_triage_reference_shares_within_two_frames_and_one_tile).

lessons.text: The static-frame regression for a rendering-only change: compare the new render with the approved one every few frames from 10-bit luma; after a 2.5 px blur no frame may differ by more than about 40 levels anywhere (a missing, doubled or wrapped word or a card drawn in another order shows 100 and more); resting tiles with real edges keep at least 95% of their crispness (the mean of their top 0.5% gradients); crispness in motion is reported; lengths must match; a region triaged as placement may be left out on named frames only.

Keep the scanners honest with positive controls: inject known faults into a still of a real render (a flash, a shimmer, a grey face, a 1 px text snap, a veil, a reversal) and require each to be flagged at its frame and nothing else; keep clips cut from real renders before their fixes and require each to be flagged in its class on at least three tiles.
A final approved from a half-scale, one-sample preview can still jitter at full samples: the stability checks run on the final render itself, and the owner's "it's so jittery" became automated tests.

terms: a half-scale, one-sample preview can hide jitter that the 16-sample final shows
destination.note: The stability gate runs on each act's final render itself.

lessons.text: Glitch triage per flag: the odd-one-out ratio d(n-1, n+1) / min(d(n-1, n), d(n, n+1)) under 0.6 means frame n is the odd one out; a block match of the 3 x 3-tile window against n±1 that explains at least 60% of the difference both ways (or equal and opposite shifts) means a feature is travelling. Categories: motion, fade, odd and look; only odd and look need eyes.

destination.note: The glitch flags' categories (motion, fade, odd, look) by the odd-one-out ratio and block matching (categorize_glitches, EXPLAINED 0.6); only odd and look need eyes.

lessons.text: The glitch scanner flags any crisp edge moving faster than about 4 px a frame and any zoom faster than about 0.5% a frame: on a clean act every flag sits inside a scheduled move.

terms: any crisp edge moving faster than about 4 px a frame
any zoom faster than about 0.5% a frame

lessons.text: Close-up probes for one moment: a crop's move per frame against a reference crop (text against its card), a crop's track through a move (an ease's tail tapers, a snapped one steps), crispness and PSNR of crops old against new, and whole-frame PSNR after a 2.5 px blur on frames where nothing moves, to show a change is rendering only. Strips enlarge crops with nearest-neighbour pixels and fixed guide lines, so a whole-pixel step shows.

destination.note: Strips enlarge one crop across frames and renders with nearest-neighbour pixels and fixed guide lines; crispness, PSNR and the 2.5 px blurred PSNR (blurred_psnr) compare crops and frames old against new.

lessons.text: A morph check: three still cards shrinking slowly on a sub-pixel spot; with the fix no edge jumps half a pixel a frame (nor 60% of the plain card's worst), every edge stays within 0.8 px of a constant offset from its true place and the content within 0.1 px; the plain card must step whole pixels, or the check has gone blind.

lessons.text: Where the type tilt goes: inside a blurred box (Chrome may raster a blurred box on its own), directly around text inside anything with an opacity below 1, a filter or a blend mode, and after a text's own transform; never on a composited layer's own transform or above one, where the compositor rotates the raster and softens it.

lessons.text: Chrome rounds away the fractional part of a box's layout offset under any transform that isn't a pure translation (a tilt), so a box centred on a fractional offset steps whole pixels: lay it out at 0 and centre it by transform, and keep a line's top on a whole pixel with the fraction in its transform.

lessons.text: What snaps and what doesn't: text and boxes placed by layout snap to whole pixels; boxes and shadows placed by transform rasterise at their exact sub-pixel positions; rotated type isn't snapped; SVG coordinates never snap.

lessons.text: Nothing in the film changes until the owner picks: proposals live in folders of their own, approved sets stay exactly as heard, and the listening file says what changes once they choose.

terms: keep everything else as it was
destination.note: A tag round's takes stay in voice/tags/<round>/ and polish trials in voice/polish/try/, pinning nothing, until the owner picks.

lessons.text: The website's section-from-layers build tooling (layer templates, placement and variant scripts, style ids, a code push with diff, and preview probes run in the site editor through its own MCP), with the website's handoff and components docs, changed after the first inventory.
sources: FILMROOT/tools/layers/ (README.md, RUNBOOK.md, *.py, probes/, templates/, configs/, records/); FILMROOT/HANDOFF.md; FILMROOT/COMPONENTS.md

destination.reason: The plan leaves the website tooling behind (docs/PLAN.md §2, "Left behind"): the section-from-layers build tools, their probes and records, and the website's handoff and components docs are about the website, not about making films.

lessons.text: A generated plate can hitch once a second where the model joins its chunks (a dropped or a frozen frame), in the vendor's own file and every conform of it. Repair the timing rather than regenerate: measure each source step's motion on the plate's moving band (Lucas-Kanade), put every source frame on a true-time axis (a missing frame takes about 1.8 units, a step more than 12% off its own ratio, a frozen frame none and its copy is dropped), make each output frame at its even place on that axis (a source frame as it is within 2%, otherwise optical-flow interpolation between its neighbours, a blend as the fallback), keep the length and the first and last frames, move tracked samples through the same warp, and stage it with its report before installing it, keeping the old sequence. ffmpeg's minterpolate can't follow an uneven time axis.

destination.note: `slate plates repair <shot>` (src/slate/gen/repair.py: steps_of, true_time, placements, warp_samples, stage, install; motion in src/slate/gen/flow.py on numpy and scipy, measured at 56 dB against 35 dB for a blend on the test texture).

terms: Put the staged frames in place, keeping the old sequence
puts the frames on a true-time axis

lessons.text: A plate passes its step check when no step is over 1.3 times the mean of its two neighbours (the films' worst after repair was 1.13, where a hitch had been 2.2); check every conformed plate and say when it hitches.

destination.note: The conform records each plate's steps in plate.json and warns when one is over 1.3× its neighbours or frozen; the repair installs only a plate that passes (repair.check).

lessons.text: Counting numbers never re-centre, refined: until the count has the final value's figures, its unseen box is the count's own shape in nines (99 while it passes 10 to 99), because a final-value box from the first frame put counts from 0 half a figure off centre (37 px); once it has them, the box is the final value, so it rests exactly where it would on its own. A suffix holds still at the box's right end, with the last figure centred in the room before it, and a word that follows the count never moves (the final value is the box for the whole count).

terms: the count's own shape in nines
holds still at the box's right end
destination.note: countShape and `followed`; golden still Kit-Section-count@7; vitest: engine/tests/kit/components.test.tsx 'boxes a count in its own nines', 'holds a count's suffix still', 'keeps a word that follows a count still'.

terms: the count's own shape in nines

lessons.text: A box that grows or settles slowly is sized by a transform, not by layout: a tile growing out of a line, a fill rising to its level, segments, an axis, ticks, dividers, drop lines, row backgrounds through a fold and an edge shadow are laid out at whole pixels and drawn to their exact place and size with translate and scale, their content counter-scaled. Laid out by height, a tile and its number settled a pixel at a time.

terms: A box that grows or settles slowly is sized by a transform too

lessons.text: Review a proposed mix against the current picture: the review copies take another mix in place of the film's own, and the film's mix and version stay as they are.

terms: The film's own mix, packet and version don't change
destination.note: `slate review --audio <mix>`: a phone cut with the timecode burned in and a half-size cut in review/proposals/, copied to Downloads for the owner's own films.

lessons.text: Before calling a stability flag a fault, check it against a synthetic perfect render of the designed motion: when it flags the same tiles, the flag is the design. One half-pixel step was a button's designed 3% press on top of the camera's slowing tail, which the render followed within 0.13 px; it stayed in the baseline with that reason rather than changing the press's ease.

terms: Before calling a flag a fault, check it against a synthetic perfect render
check it against a perfect render of the designed motion

lessons.text: Before re-rendering a fix, take the fault's flags out of the act's stability baseline, so the new render proves the fix instead of the baseline hiding the fault.

terms: instead of the baseline hiding the fault
destination.note: `slate qa stability baseline --act N --drop F[-F] [--drop-class C] --by NAME --reason TEXT`.

terms: Take the fault's flags out of the baseline before you re-render the fix

lessons.text: A review cut goes out only when every installed act passes its regression and stability checks with no reversal and no wobble, every resolved flag is written down with its reason, and the 0.5 s contact sheets have been read end to end with nothing blank, broken or out of order.

terms: Every installed act passes its regression and stability checks with no reversal and no wobble
You've read the 0.5-second contact sheets end to end
